youtube_title: Westville, Indiana: the prison that began as a state mental hospital (Westville request)
youtube:
You asked for Westville! Before it was a prison, the Westville Correctional Facility was Beatty Memorial Hospital, a state mental hospital that opened in February 1951 for patients from 17 northern Indiana counties. In 1954 it opened a maximum security division for patients the state called criminally insane, from all over Indiana; the first were moved there from the old Hospital for Insane Criminals at the state prison in Michigan City. After Indiana prisoners sued over crowded prisons, lawmakers voted in 1977 to turn the hospital into a prison. The last patients left in the summer of 1979, and it became the Westville Correctional Center. Now a new prison is going up next door, due to open in 2027, and parts of the old campus are set to come down. It's an active prison: please view it only from the road. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Westville #LaPorteCounty #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

Sources: Indiana Archives and Records Administration; Indiana Department of Correction (facility history, 2019 audit report, history book); Indiana Department of Administration; Indiana Historical Society; LaPorte Herald-Dispatch; The Indiana Lawyer; ABC57 (2026); Elevatus Architecture.
